items.message: Content written into `recorded.content` originates from the cassette entry without any size bound. An attacker or insider who controls a cassette file (or a CI artifact that feeds into harvest) can embed an arbitrarily large string that then travels into a case file stored in the repository and is later read back in full by `eval run`. This is a storage/resource concern that crosses a trust boundary, not a sanitisation absence — but the same field also flows through `_as_answer(str(case.recorded…[truncated]

The tamper-detection check (declared key vs actual key) is skipped when `declared` is empty, meaning a case with no `harvested.key` field but with a `recorded` block is graded without verifying that the request and answer belong together. An editor who removes or omits the `key` field from a case file causes the integrity check to be silently bypassed on line 1041 (`if declared and declared != actual`).
